item.title: Frank and Dyche on standby! - Crystal Palace consider managerial alternatives as Pierre Sage fights to save his job
item.description: Pierre Sage - (C)Getty Images Pierre Sage’s tenure at Selhurst Park is hanging by a thread following a bruising 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool. The result leaves Crystal Palace rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table as the club enters the final international break of the calendar year. Palace weigh up managerial change after dismal run The hierarchy at Crystal Palace are currently deliberating the future of Pierre Sage after a catastrophic start to the Premier League campaign. Sunday’s home defeat to Liverpool marked a fourth consecutive league loss, leaving the Eagles with just seven points from their opening ten fixtures. The club is currently struggling with the worst defensive record in the top flight, having shipped 24 goals already this term, while their European form has also stuttered with only one win from four Europa League matches. According to Sky Sports , Former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank has emerged as a leading candidate to take over as manager should a change be made. Sage, who arrived with high expectations after leading Lens to a historic French Cup victory, has found the transition to English football incredibly difficult. Despite the mounting pressure, he remained defiant following the latest setback at Selhurst Park. "It's not from the dream to the nightmare," the 47-year-old insisted. "I'm not feeling this. I'm just in my job, and focusing on my job, and what I have to do to find the solution. The results are not at this level, and I know I have to push more on those things, especially in our way of playing, to make that move." Tactical identity crisis and recruitment struggles A significant part of the problem appears to be a clash between Sage’s preferred philosophy and the current profile of the squad. At Lens, Sage built a reputation for high-tempo pressing and dominance in possession, but the Eagles have struggled to replicate that intensity. The squad has missed the spark provided by Ismaila Sarr, whose absence through injury has been harshly felt after he scored 21 goals last season. Sage has also been forced to deal with off-field distractions regarding the futures of Jean-Philippe Mateta and Sarr, both of whom have been linked with exits. This combination of bad luck and tactical misalignment has seen Palace winless in the league since mid-October. Reflecting on the current situation, the manager admitted the gap between their output and expectations. "We have to be more competitive," Sage explained to The media. "At the moment, we create some things, we expect a lot of things, but we don't have the results expected." Potential candidates waiting in the wings With the international break providing a natural window for change, the Palace board is considering immediate alternatives. Along with Frank, former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche is also believed to have supporters within the club's leadership. item.title: Elias Lindholm scores 1st of Boston’s 3 goals in 1st period, carrying Bruins past Panthers, 4-1
item.description: Boston Bruins' Elias Lindholm (28) shoots and scores past Florida Panthers' Aaron Ekblad (5) during the first period of an NHL hockey game Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, in Boston. (AP Photo/CJ Gunther) CJ Gunther Elias Lindholm, Mikey Eyssimont and Morgan Geekie each scored a goal in an opening period that started out testy, carrying the Boston Bruins past the Florida Panthers 4-1 on Sunday. Jeremy Swayman made 40 saves, 17 coming in the first period, for the Bruins, who improved to 7-0-0 at home by winning their fourth straight game a day after placing young star James Hagens on injured reserve. JJ Peterka added a goal for Boston, which owns a plus-21 goal differential at TD Garden. David Pastrnak and Pavel Zacha each added two assists. Carter Verhaeghe scored a power-play goal for the Panthers, and Jacob Markstrom stopped 32 shots. Florida has lost three of four games. Boston’s 6-foot-7 defenseman Nikita Zadorov dropped the gloves against 6-foot-1 forward Brady Tkachuk at the opening faceoff, setting the stage for 126 total penalty minutes. Just over six minutes later, Florida’s Garnet Hathaway squared off against forward Mark Kastelic. The Panthers swept the three games against Boston last season, winning each by one goal. Following a lengthy review, Lindholm was credited with a goal that made it 1-0 just 4:50 into the game after his wrister broke off Markstrom and trickled behind him, nearing the goal line as he attempted to pull it back with his glove. Eyssimont poked a loose puck into the net following his wraparound shot, making it 2-0 less than two minutes later. Geekie then scored for the fourth straight game, one-timing a shot for a power-play goal at 15:59 with the Bruins on a two-man advantage. Verhaeghe’s one-timer cut it to 3-1. The Bruins, who entered with the NHL’s second-best goal differential behind Carolina, were off since rolling to a 6-2 victory at Pittsburgh on Thursday. item.title: Aidan Hutchinson Sends Emotional Message to Jack Campbell After Lions Win
item.description: The Detroit Lions picked up a 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon, but following the game, defensive end Aidan Hutchinson made it clear that one of his teammates was never far from his thoughts. During his postgame interview with Melanie Collins of CBS Sports, Hutchinson delivered an emotional message to hospitalized linebacker Jack Campbell, who continues recovering from the frightening neck injury he suffered against Minnesota last weekend. “Jack, we love you brother. We know you’re watching. Miss you, man,” Hutchinson said. It was a short message, but one that spoke volumes about what Campbell means to his teammates. "Jack, we love you brother. We know you're watching. Miss you, man." Aidan Hutchinson sent hospitalized teammate Jack Campbell a message after the @Lions win 🎤 @Melanie_Collins pic.twitter.com/sXaleMszsf — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 8, 2026 Aidan Hutchinson Sends Message to Jack Campbell The emotional moment came during Hutchinson’s on-field interview following Detroit’s victory at Hard Rock Stadium. The NFL on CBS shared Hutchinson’s message shortly after the game, highlighting the bond between two of Detroit’s most important defensive players. Campbell suffered his injury during the fourth quarter of Detroit’s November 1 victory over the Minnesota Vikings and has remained a major focus of the team’s attention throughout the week. As we previously reported following Campbell’s personal statement , the linebacker revealed that he has full movement in his lower body and continues making progress with movement in his upper body. While those developments have been encouraging, Campbell’s recovery remains the priority. Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) reacts after linebacker Jack Campbell (not pictured) was injured during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Continue Rallying Around Jack Campbell Hutchinson’s message was just the latest example of the support Campbell has received from his teammates. Before Sunday’s matchup, defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard and members of Detroit’s linebacker group arrived at Hard Rock Stadium wearing No. 46 jerseys in honor of Campbell. As we reported earlier Sunday , the Lions shared photos of the tribute with a simple message: “For 4️⃣6️⃣.” The gesture demonstrated just how much Campbell means to the entire organization. And after Sunday’s victory, Hutchinson made sure his injured teammate knew he was still part of the celebration. The Lions will continue preparing for their upcoming games while Campbell focuses on his recovery. But one thing is clear. Jack Campbell may not be on the field with his teammates right now, but he’s certainly not forgotten.

item.title: Freiburg third after beating Union, Leverkusen beat Cologne in derby
item.description: Freiburg's Japanese midfielder Yuito Suzuki scored in his side's 2-0 win over Union Berlin on Sunday. (Silas Stein) Freiburg kept hot on the heels of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund with a comfortable 2-0 home win over lowly Union Berlin to return to third in the Bundesliga table on Sunday, while Bayer Leverkusen sunk derby rivals Cologne. Freiburg pressured Union captain Rani Khedira into an own goal nine minutes after half-time and Yuito Suzuki scored another as the hosts won despite their own skipper Vincenzo Grifo missing a penalty. Last season's beaten Europa League finalists are third on 19 points, two behind Bayern and Dortmund with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference. "We knew our chances would come and we managed to convert them well," Freiburg winger Derry Scherhant told DAZN. After an even first-half, Freiburg were impressive after the break and forced a last-ditch intervention from Khedira, who knocked the ball into his own net. Scherhant chipped for Suzuki to score with 67 minutes gone. The Black Forest side may have won by a higher margin were it not for Union goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow, who kept out Grifo's 84th-minute penalty and made a number of other saves. Earlier on Sunday, goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne which lifted the visitors to fifth in the table. The fiery encounter produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the home side. One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart. The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated. Leverkusen broke the deadlock just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on. Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide. Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half. Schick had a goal ruled out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league appearances this season. Germany winger Said El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback and left the hosts stranded in 15th, two points above Union who sit in the relegation play-off spot. In Sunday's late game, Hoffenheim won 2-1 at promoted Schalke, with Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle getting on the scoresheet for the hosts. dwi/td/lp

item.title: Lane Kiffin falls to 0-6 against Alabama despite pink locker room trick
item.description: The Alabama Crimson Tide dressed in Lane Kiffin’s pink visiting locker room at Tiger Stadium on Saturday and walked out with a 31-13 win over the LSU Tigers. No visitor had won in Baton Rouge this season, and Alabama became the first to win after using the room Kiffin had painted this fall. Kiffin took the idea from Iowa, where Hayden Fry painted the Kinnick Stadium visitors’ quarters pink after arriving in 1979, and he used it at Ole Miss before coming to LSU. He explained the choice at his Oct. 12 news conference, which 247Sports transcribed. “We did that at the last place, and I think we did it about two years ago. We never lost a home game. We haven’t lost a home game yet. Maybe it works. That’s why,” Kiffin said . Oct 24, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin looks on during the second quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images LSU outgained Alabama 457-285 and led with 16 minutes to play. It lost by 18 because it went 0-for-4 on fourth down, missed a field goal and turned the ball over in Alabama territory, and Alabama turned those empty trips into a 14-0 fourth quarter. NEW: Lane Kiffin had LSU’s visiting locker room painted pink in October. The theory is that the color helps reduce visitingplayers’ aggression and energy levels. (via @yea_ala) https://t.co/WbU77o8mw9 — On3 (@On3) November 7, 2026 Where did LSU’s afternoon slip away? The most debated call came with eight minutes left, when Kiffin kept his offense on the field on fourth-and-10 from the LSU 25. “And then at the end of the game, you can play to just keep the score low when you’re on your own 20, but you have no chance to win by punting really, analytically, so you go for it,” Kiffin said. Alabama’s version of the afternoon centered on those same stops. Keelon Russell played through an ankle injury and threw three touchdown passes, and Kalen DeBoer opened his postgame news conference with the defense, in remarks On3 transcribed. “Just super proud of the guys. Team win all around. Defense coming up with some big stops. I believe they were 0-for-4 on fourth down and got us some field position, and offense taking advantage of that when we did,” DeBoer said . Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen Deboer talks on the sideline Thursday, Jan. 1, 2026, during the Rose Bowl and quarterfinal game of the College Football Playoff against Indiana Hoosiers at Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena, Calif. Alabama has now won seven of its last eight games at Tiger Stadium, including a 42-13 rout there in 2024 before any of the walls changed color. The paint gave Kiffin a talking point and his visitors a strange pregame setting, and Saturday showed how little either one counts once a team comes up empty on four fourth downs. The loss dropped LSU to 6-3 and 5-1 at home, and its playoff hopes now depend on help from elsewhere with the Texas Longhorns coming to Baton Rouge next. item.title: 'Everyone knows how to play on a green wicket': Kusal Mendis backs Sri Lanka batters to tackle Pakistan's pace challenge
item.description: Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis is confident his experienced batting line-up has the technique and temperament to counter Pakistan's expected pace-friendly conditions as the visitors prepare for the opening Test in Rawalpindi on Monday. With the hosts potentially opting for a greener surface to bring their fast bowlers into the contest, Mendis has backed his senior batters to rise to the challenge, insisting their experience of playing in England will hold them in good stead. The Sri Lankan skipper believes the presence of experienced campaigners such as Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva, alongside himself, gives the team the necessary confidence to negotiate challenging conditions away from home. "We know they will be giving a little bit different wicket. I think the batters have to manage our skills and preparation well. I know we have a very good batting line-up with some very senior players... Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva, myself, and a couple of other guys. "Everyone knows how to play on a green wicket. We played really well in England also, so I have no doubt in my batting line-up," Mendis told reporters. First Test assignment as captain for Kusal Mendis The Rawalpindi Test will mark Mendis' first assignment as Sri Lanka's Test captain after he took over the leadership from Dhananjaya de Silva in early October. The 31-year-old admitted that leading the side in the longest format was something he was particularly looking forward to, despite the challenges of an extended stay in Pakistan. Sri Lanka have spent more than a month in the country, having arrived for the preceding white-ball assignments. Mendis acknowledged that spending such a long period away from home, largely between hotels and training sessions, had not been easy for the players. However, he said the squad had found ways to keep itself occupied and was now fully focused on switching gears for Test cricket. "Honestly, compared to ODIs and T20s, Test cricket is very different. I think everyone mostly likes to play Test cricket. Me as well. I'm very happy to captain in Test cricket," he said. "It's not easy, sometimes we stay in the hotel and come to practice and that's it... I think it's a little bit hard to stay one month in a hotel. But we do some stuff in the team room, games and individual things to keep ourselves entertained." Mendis backs experienced bowling attack to deliver Sri Lanka are yet to register a Test victory in their two series this year against West Indies and India, but Mendis believes the performances of his bowling unit offer plenty of encouragement ahead of the Pakistan challenge. The skipper pointed to the experience within the attack, highlighting how the fast bowlers have delivered consistently across formats and are equipped to handle the demands of Test cricket. item.description: Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals were closing in on a win in Madrid when the stadium suddenly stole the spotlight by losing it. item.title: Dan Campbell explains decision to bench Christian Mahogany
item.description: Detroit Lions guard Christian Mahogany (73) walks of the field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Tuesday, July 22, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions made a very surprising personnel decision in their 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins. Lions coach Dan Campbell decided to give Miles Frazier his first career start at left guard over Christian Mahogany. There weren’t any indications that Mahogany’s play had dipped—in fact, he was nationally praised for his performance against the Vikings —so his benching came as a complete surprise. After the Lions’ win, Campbell explained the decision, noting it was a disciplinary action. “That was team rules (for) Mahogany. It was really that simple,” Campbell said. “Miles deserved his opportunity, so he got it. Doesn’t mean it stays that way, but that was the way it was going to be today.” In his first career start, Frazier clearly struggled in the first half, giving up several early pressures to Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler. He did settle down in the second half, though, helping the Lions score on every second-half possession—outside of the last drive that bled the remainder of the clock. Still, there will be plenty of questions going forward about what exactly Mahogany did to earn a benching. Not only was he getting national praise and passing the eye test, but he has earned PFF’s 10th-highest grade among guards with at least 130 snaps. Hopefully, he can get back in the Lions’ good graces and continue his strong season.

item.title: Feyi-Waboso burns bright as England energy endorses Borthwick
item.description: "Plastic energy." That's what Bongi Mbonambi described it as. After scraping past Steve Borthwick's side in the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final, the South Africa hooker was scathing of England's back-slapping and celebrating of in-game wins. By then, it had already become something of a meme. Back row Ben Earl pumping his fist to celebrate Ireland's crooked line-out throw in a pre-tournament warm-up was a particular source of online mockery. But, while it isn't the diesel grunt that can win matches on its own, "plastic energy" is still something. It is the body language that shows mindset and intent, that a team's pilot light is on and burning bright. England had it under Borthwick at the Stade de France three years ago, coming agonisingly close to derailing the Springboks. And they had it in spades in Sunday's 45-22 win against the Wallabies. Earl, inevitably, was one outlet, loudly celebrating a third-minute scrum success. But there were plenty more examples throughout the match. Jamie George bellowing into the stands after the opening score; captain Maro Itoje being surrounded with congratulations after an early charge-down; Henry Slade being embraced after a lung-busting late try-saving tackle on Max Jorgensen. Borthwick needed it all. A report in the Times newspaper earlier in the week had said that a rift between the players and their coach opened in Argentina in July, at the end of the summer's campaign. England's senior players denied it. Nothing more to see, they said, than the transparent honesty of a team where input is valued and improvement is the lodestar. But, they also promised proof on the pitch against Australia. It was a risky gambit. Another misfiring, disjointed, underpowered performance – like that in their most-recent visit to Twickenham, February's 42-21 defeat by Ireland - would dial up the pressure on Borthwick another notch. Instead, his fired-up players turned up. They did so in the obvious ways. There was gainline physicality, breakdown bravery and crunching physicality.
